  %\VignetteIndexEntry{15. Hydro modification}

---

Hydro Modify follows Survey Events in the Study tabset. It uses the selected
Event and its existing Stream DEM editions. `selected_group()` in Event settings
resolves a valid explicit selection or the first saved Event before the hidden
dropdown renders. Both panels therefore use the same context; pending edits still
withhold processing, and no saved Events produce the normal empty state.
Hydro Modify shows the selected Event date above its Stream tabs. The current implementation supports
close inspection, persistent cutline drawing, background hydro modification and
review of the saved result against the original DEM.

`survey_event_settings_server()` exposes its saved Event context to
`hydro_modify_server()` through `mod_study_server()`. Each Stream tab resolves its
eligible edition with `dem_request()` and `find_dem()`. Event, Study or Stream
changes replace the map context and restore drawings bound to that source edition.

The map widget itself is initialized to the DEM raster's extent; it does not
depend on an early proxy command reaching a still-hidden widget. The layer control
selects Imagery, Street map or OpenTopoMap and independently toggles Elevation,
Hillshade, Cutlines and DEM extent. Stream changes replace the map widget and
restore only drawings attached to that displayed DEM. Do not queue proxy clears
of the cutline group during replacement: Shiny may deliver them after the new
widget has restored its saved lines, erasing those lines from the browser.
`add_opentopomap()` supplies consistent provider attribution and native zoom
limits across all interactive viewers, using the Hydro basemap pane here. Study
workspace layer-control refreshes retain the basemap choices even with no overlays.
Independent Elevation and Hillshade opacity sliders in the lower-left map control
adjust their panes immediately in the browser. Values survive Stream/map
replacement within the page; they do not trigger raster work or change cutlines.

The display worker starts and loads spatial packages when a Survey Event context
is available, before map bounds are needed. Map bounds are debounced before it calls
`fluvgeo::prepare_hydro_dem_view()`. It crops a file-backed DEM before preparing
elevation and hillshade display GeoTIFFs. Study-local `terrain-display` caches
contain COG elevation and hillshade pyramids, keyed by source path, size, modified
time and display recipe. The interactive caller sets `build_cache=FALSE`: it reuses
existing pyramids but does not wait for a full-raster cache build. With no cache,
GDAL reads only a bounded, display-sized window and hillshade is calculated on
that window (at display resolution for overview scales). The default backend
option still supports explicit full-cache preparation outside the interactive
path. GDAL window extraction selects available overviews within a display
budget; close views retain source cells before Web Mercator display
reprojection. Geographic map bounds are intersected with the DEM's geographic
extent before projection to its local CRS. Wrapped longitudes are normalized;
empty views return a normal message and a Return to Stream action. Each viewport
uses a local elevation stretch. The color sequence
matches `fluvgeo::get_terrain_leaflet()` and is shared by the other DEM views.
International-foot elevations on metre grids are converted for hillshade slope.
Analytical DEMs are never changed by display preparation.

A cold-worker check on a saved mainstem Hydro DEM measured 9.43 seconds for the
window-only first view versus 45.76 seconds when first building full-raster
pyramids. Worker prewarming can overlap package startup with Event navigation;
timing still depends on the source, storage and machine.

The line/edit/delete toolbar is available when the display is unaggregated and
the map shows at least two screen pixels per source cell. This is an inspection
aid, not a claim that a blockage has been resolved. Completed Leaflet drawings
are validated as geographic polylines and saved immediately. A revision conflict
rejects a stale edit rather than overwriting another saved drawing.

| Data object / preparation asset | Operation | Storage and ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Saved Stream DEM | Read for display | Existing external GeoTIFF edition associated with the selected Event and Stream |
| Cutline drawing revision | `hydro_drawn_lines()`, `study_hydro_store()` | Study-local `hydro-modify/<event hash>/<stream hash>/<revision>/cutlines.gpkg`, layer `cutlines`; source DEM ID and context in `cutlines.rds` |
| Hydro-modified Stream DEM | `launch_hydro_burn()` -> `fluvgeo::burn_hydro_cutlines()` -> `hydro_publish()` | Drawing revision's `result/hydro-dem.tif`, `provenance.json` and internal `result.rds`; explicit source DEM edition and cutline revision links |
| Elevation and hillshade display | `prepare_hydro_dem_view()` | Session/job-owned temporary GeoTIFFs, removed when replaced or the session ends |
| Display pyramids | `.fg_hydro_display_cache()` | Study-local `terrain-display/<key>` COGs and completion record; regenerable, separate from analytical editions |

These drawings are local preparation assets, not an implemented FGDB portable
hydro-DEM binding. Earlier revisions and source DEMs are retained. Empty drawing
revisions have no vector payload. Completed derived rasters are published by
renaming their job directory only after completion. A changed drawing, displayed
source, source selection or Study context rejects stale completion. A newer DEM
edition does not invalidate a job bound to the retained displayed edition. Reopening
drawings selects their linked edition when its saved input binding remains valid.
Display/hydro-only backend releases reuse equivalent Stream DEM recipes rather
than trigger unnecessary rebuilding. Re-applying
an unchanged drawing reuses its saved result. Changing drawings creates a new
revision and switches review back to the original DEM until the new cuts are
applied. Editing and source changes retain previous results.

The author-provided legacy `_02_HydroDEM.py` rasterizes line IDs, optionally
expands zones, calculates each zone's minimum elevation, and replaces elevations
inside those zones. The owner authorized a comparable terra cell assignment on
2026-09-29. The implementation uses touched cells, lowest drawing-order ID for
shared cells, and no widening. Source NoData is preserved, including within a cut.
Cutlines crossing only NoData are reported by number and omitted, while valid
cuts are applied; if all cuts lack elevations, no result is published. A rectangular
raster extent is not a valid-cell footprint. Fully covered cutlines are recorded
without failing the operation. Rasterization uses an explicit zero
background, excluded from zonal minima; file-backed integer rasterization must
not rely on implicit NoData background behavior. Native terra operations do the
file-backed work. Zone calculations use the cutline envelope, padded by one
source cell and aligned to the source grid. A file-backed merge restores this
patch over the full source; the final writer explicitly restores elevation units
and CRS. No full DEM values are materialized in R. Basemaps occupy a fixed pane
below hillshade and elevation, so switching basemaps cannot cover the DEM or
cutlines.

On the retained 8,974 by 10,688-cell mainstem DEM with one saved cutline,
the background worker took 12.27 seconds versus 37.12 seconds for full-grid
zone intermediates on the development workstation. Complete raster comparison
verified identical values and NoData, with matching grid, units, zone minima and
source checksum. This is a local benchmark, not a general runtime guarantee;
the final full-resolution output still needs writing and hashing.

The output retains the source grid, CRS and elevation units. JSON evidence records
source/output SHA-256 hashes, zone minima, method, software, source execution
history and the exact PROJ operation used to place map-digitized XY cutlines on
the grid. This display-coordinate conversion does not execute a new DEM datum
transformation. Full datum-operation selection for new DEM references remains a
separate workflow. This local result is not a qualified FGDB portable delivery.

Verification routes: `test-hydro-modify.R` exercises drawing validation, revision
conflicts and reopening; `test-hydro-module.R` exercises Event/Stream binding;
`test-hydro-publication.R` checks completion and stale-job rejection. Backend
`test_burn_hydro_cutlines.R` independently checks expected cells and intersections;
`test_hydro_dem_view.R` covers world/wrapped/outside viewports.
Real-window display checks use existing DEMs without writing analyst cutlines.
Browser review is still required for the rendered drawing interactions.
